title: Free-radical substitution
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR07#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR07#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR07#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR07#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR07#N.2, OR07#N.6, OR07#N.9, OR07#N.12, OR07#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Homolytic fission
items.clue: A bond breaks so that one electron goes to each atom.

items.label: Radical
items.clue: A species with an unpaired electron, marked by a dot; highly reactive.

items.label: Propagation
items.clue: Chain stage in which the reactive species is regenerated, so the two steps repeat.

items.label: Termination
items.clue: Stage in which two reactive species combine and are removed, e.g. giving a trace of ethane.

questions.stem: Which statement about the chlorine radical, Cl•, is correct?

options.text: It has a 1− charge, which the dot is there to show.
It has eight outer electrons, all paired, like the chloride ion.
It is neutral, with seven outer electrons, one of them unpaired.
It is unreactive, as it has only one unpaired electron.

questions.explanation: Chlorine has seven outer electrons: three pairs and one unpaired electron. The dot marks the unpaired one. There is no charge.

questions.stem: Methane reacts with bromine in ultraviolet (UV) light. Which equation represents the initiation step?

options.text: Br₂ → Br⁺ + Br⁻
CH₄ → CH₃• + H•
Br₂ → Br• + Br•
CH₄ → CH₃⁻ + H⁺

questions.explanation: UV light breaks the Br–Br bond homolytically: one electron of the bonding pair goes to each atom, giving two bromine radicals.

questions.stem: 2,2-dimethylpropane, C₅H₁₂, reacts with chlorine in UV light. Four steps of the mechanism are: P: C₅H₁₁• + Cl₂ → C₅H₁₁Cl + Cl• Q: Cl₂ → 2Cl• R: C₅H₁₁• + Cl• → C₅H₁₁Cl S: C₅H₁₂ + Cl• → C₅H₁₁• + HCl Which sequence gives initiation, then the two propagation steps in the order they happen, then termination?

options.text: Q, P, S, R
S, Q, P, R
Q, S, P, R
Q, S, R, P

questions.explanation: Q makes Cl•. In S, Cl• removes an H atom, giving C₅H₁₁•. In P, that radical takes a Cl atom from Cl₂ and regenerates Cl•. R, two radicals combining, is termination.

questions.stem: The products of the reaction of methane with chlorine in UV light include CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄. How are most of these more highly substituted products formed?

options.text: Cl• removes an H atom from a chloromethane; the radical then reacts with Cl₂
Cl• replaces an H atom in a chloromethane directly, releasing a free H• radical
Chlorinated methyl radicals combine with Cl• in termination, the main source of products
Each forms in one step, e.g. CH₃Cl + Cl₂ → CH₂Cl₂ + HCl, as its equation shows

questions.explanation: Cl• attacks C–H bonds in chloromethanes as it does in methane: CH₃Cl + Cl• → CH₂Cl• + HCl, then CH₂Cl• + Cl₂ → CH₂Cl₂ + Cl•. Repeating gives CHCl₃ and CCl₄.

questions.stem: A mixture of methane and chlorine does not react in the dark. A single brief flash of UV light splits a few Cl₂ molecules, yet many CH₃Cl molecules form for each Cl₂ split. Which explains this?

options.text: The flash heats the gas, and the hot gas keeps reacting after the light stops.
UV light breaks C–H bonds in methane, and each H• released starts a new reaction.
Each Cl• formed swaps places with one H atom in methane and is then used up.
Each Cl• starts a chain, as propagation regenerates Cl• again and again.

questions.explanation: CH₄ + Cl• → CH₃• + HCl, then CH₃• + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + Cl•. The chain repeats many times until two radicals meet in termination.
